inline_comments.comment: Three `console.log` calls are left in `buildModuleGraph` — these are clearly debugging artifacts that must not be merged. Per project conventions, all diagnostic logging in Node.js server-side code should use `logger` from `storybook/internal/node-logger` (already imported at the top of this file) rather than `console.*`. The entire block at lines 98-107 should be removed.

`bail()` calls `server?.watcher.off('change', watcherChangeHandler)`, but the handler is registered at line 161 with `server.watcher.on('all', watcherChangeHandler)`. Because `'change'` and `'all'` are separate Chokidar event channels, this `off` call is a no-op — the `'all'` listener is never removed. After `bail()`, any subsequent file-system events continue to fire the handler (though `listeners.clear()` makes notifications harmless), but the dangling listener prevents the watcher from being properly released and causes a resource leak across server restarts. Change this to `server?.watcher.off('all', watcherChangeHandler)` to match the registration.

`waitForModuleGraph` is declared with `const` inside `start()`, making it inaccessible to `bail()`. If `bail()` is called while the interval is still polling (i.e., before `fileToModulesMap` is populated), the interval continues to run indefinitely. In that scenario, once the condition is eventually met, `await server.waitForRequestsIdle()` will be called on an already-closed server, likely throwing an error. Move `waitForModuleGraph` to module scope (alongside `debounce` and `watcherChangeHandler`) and add a corresponding `clearInterval` call in `bail()` so it can be cancelled reliably.

`setInterval(async () => { ... })` passes an async callback, but `setInterval` does not handle the returned Promise — any rejection (e.g., `server.waitForRequestsIdle()` throwing after the server is closed) is silently swallowed with no error surfaced. Wrap the async body in a void-returning IIFE with its own try-catch so errors can be logged or forwarded to listeners: `setInterval(() => { void (async () => { try { ... } catch (err) { ... } })(); }, 1000)`.
Per project coding guidelines, all `vi.mock()` calls in test files must include the `{ spy: true }` option. Change to: `vi.mock('./vite-server', { spy: true })`.

The assertion `expect(fakeViteServer.watcher.off).toHaveBeenCalledWith('change', expect.any(Function))` checks for the `'change'` event, but the implementation registers the handler with `server.watcher.on('all', watcherChangeHandler)`. This assertion validates the wrong event name and would pass even though the real cleanup (removing from `'all'`) never happens — the test confirms a bug rather than catching it. Change the expected event to `'all'` to match the registration.

general_comments.comment: `buildModuleGraph` is a pure transformation utility with no dependency on builder lifecycle state — it converts Vite's internal `fileToModulesMap` into the builder-agnostic `ModuleGraph` type. Exporting it from `index.ts` (the builder entry point) conflates infrastructure concerns with data transformation logic and unnecessarily widens the module's public API surface. Consider moving it to a dedicated file such as `./utils/build-module-graph.ts` and re-exporting it only if external consumers genuinely need it, keeping `index.ts` focused on the builder lifecycle (`start`, `bail`, `onModuleGraphChange`).
